column1: regress§The analysis regresses yield on rainfall and nothing else.§这项分析只把产量对降雨做**回归**。
regressive§A regressive change to the font made the whole page harder.§字体上一次**倒退**的改动让整页都更难读。
regularly§He wrote regularly for forty years and published twice.§他**坚持**写了四十年，只出版过两次。
regulate§Nothing regulates the temperature here except the window.§这里除了窗户，没有任何东西能**调节**温度。
rehabilitation§Rehabilitation of the reputation began with one careful article.§名誉的**恢复**始于一篇审慎的文章。
rehash§A rehash of last year's plan arrived with a new cover.§去年计划的**老调重弹**换了个新封面就来了。
rehearsal§A dress rehearsal exists to find the problems nobody predicted.§**彩排**的意义在于找出谁也没预料到的问题。
rehearse§He rehearsed the refusal and delivered it badly anyway.§他把拒绝的话**排练**过，说出来还是很糟。
reinforce§Praise reinforces whatever behaviour happened to precede it.§表扬会**强化**碰巧发生在它之前的任何行为。
reintegrate§Reintegrating the two catalogues took three people a year.§把两份目录**重新整合**，三个人花了一年。
reiterate§Let me reiterate the one point that keeps getting lost.§让我**重申**那个总是被忽略的一点。
rejection§A rejection letter kept for thirty years is a kind of trophy.§一封保存了三十年的**拒信**是一种战利品。
rejuvenate§Nothing rejuvenates a syllabus like a genuinely new question.§没有什么比一个真正的新问题更能让教学大纲**焕发生机**。
release§The valve releases pressure before it becomes a problem.§这个阀门在压力成为问题之前就把它**释放**掉。
relegate§Two beloved subjects were relegated to an optional week.§两门受欢迎的科目被**降格**为可选的一周。
relevance§Relevance is a judgement, not a property of the document.§**相关性**是一种判断，而不是文件本身的属性。
relieve§A short walk relieved a headache three tablets had not.§一次短暂的散步**缓解**了三片药都没缓解的头痛。
relinquish§Nobody relinquishes a room in a building this crowded.§在这么拥挤的楼里，没人会**让出**一个房间。
relish§He ate the same lunch for thirty years with evident relish.§三十年来他吃着同样的午餐，显然**乐在其中**。
relocate§Relocating the colony was cheaper than protecting it.§**迁移**这个族群比保护它更便宜。
reluctant§A reluctant witness is often the most accurate one.§**不情愿的**证人往往最准确。
remedial§Remedial classes were held in the room with the best light.§**补习课**安排在光线最好的房间。
remedy§The remedy proposed was worse than the complaint.§提出的**补救**办法比抱怨本身更糟。
reminiscence§A reminiscence recorded at eighty is not a document of youth.§八十岁时录下的**回忆**，不是青年时代的文献。
reminiscent§The layout is reminiscent of a much older publication.§这个版式**让人想起**一份古老得多的出版物。
remiss§I have been remiss about answering and I apologize.§我一直**疏于回复**，在此致歉。
remnant§A remnant of the population survives on two islands.§这个种群的**残余**在两座岛上存活下来。
remonstrance§A written remonstrance is harder to ignore than a spoken one.§书面的**抗议**比口头的更难被忽视。
remonstrate§He remonstrated gently and got exactly what he wanted.§他温和地**据理力争**，得到了他想要的一切。
remorseful§A remorseful tone in an apology is what makes it one.§道歉里的**悔意**，正是它成其为道歉的原因。
remuneration§Remuneration in kind is harder to tax and harder to refuse.§实物**报酬**更难征税，也更难拒绝。
renew§Her interest renewed itself every time she reread the letters.§每次重读那些信，她的兴趣都会**重新燃起**。
renewal§Urban renewal removed the buildings and kept the street names.§城市**更新**拆掉了建筑，保留了街名。
renounce§To renounce a method publicly takes more courage than adopting one.§公开**放弃**一种方法，比采用一种方法更需要勇气。
renovation§Renovation revealed a doorway bricked up in 1840.§**翻修**中发现了一道一八四〇年被砌死的门。
renowned§Renowned for one thing, she spent her life on another.§她因一件事**出名**，一生却花在另一件事上。
renunciation§Renunciation of violence was the precondition for the talks.§**放弃**暴力是会谈的前提。
reparation§Reparation of the wall took four masons and one summer.§**修复**这道墙用了四名泥瓦匠和一个夏天。
repeal§Repeal is easier than reform and rarely as useful.§**废止**比改革容易，却很少同样有用。
repel§Two magnets repel each other with a force you can feel.§两块磁铁以一种能感觉到的力互相**排斥**。
repentance§Repentance is measured in behaviour, not in adjectives.§**悔改**是用行为衡量的，不是用形容词。
repertory§A repertory company performs six plays in rotation.§一个**保留剧目**剧团轮演六出戏。
repetitive§Repetitive strain builds up for years before it announces itself.§**重复**性劳损积累多年才显现出来。
replica§A replica of the boat was rowed across in 1994.§一九九四年，一艘**复制的船**被划过了海峡。
replicate§The pattern replicates itself at three different scales.§这种图案在三种不同尺度上**重复出现**。
replication§Replication is the least glamorous and most necessary work.§**重复验证**是最不光鲜也最必要的工作。
reprehensible§What is reprehensible in a colleague is a scandal in a stranger.§同事身上**应受谴责**的事，换成陌生人就是丑闻。
repress§A repressed detail returns in the third telling.§**被压下去**的细节在第三次讲述时又冒了出来。
repressive§Repressive silence is easy to mistake for consent.§**压抑的**沉默很容易被误认为同意。
reprieve§A last-minute reprieve arrived by telegram.§最后一刻的**缓刑**令是用电报发来的。
reproduce§The species reproduces only in water above twelve degrees.§这种生物只在十二度以上的水中**繁殖**。
reproduction§Reproduction rights cost more than the photographs did.§**复制**权的费用比照片本身还贵。
repudiate§He repudiated the debt and the court disagreed.§他**拒不承认**这笔债务，法院不同意。
reputable§A reputable source is one that publishes its corrections.§**可靠**的来源，是会公布自己更正的来源。
requisition§A requisition form for a pencil ran to two pages.§领一支铅笔的**申领单**有两页长。
rescind§They rescinded the invitation without giving a reason.§他们**撤回**了邀请，没有给出理由。
researcher§A researcher's best month is usually her third.§**研究者**最好的一个月通常是第三个月。
resemble§Nothing in the copy resembles the urgency of the original.§副本里没有任何东西**像原件**那样带着急切。
resentment§Resentment is the tax on a favour never acknowledged.§**怨恨**是对一份从未被承认的恩情所征的税。
residual§Residual doubt is not the same as reasonable doubt.§**残留**的疑虑与合理怀疑不是一回事。
resilience§Resilience is a property of systems, not of individuals.§**恢复力**是系统的属性，不是个人的。
resilient§A resilient schedule has slack built into it.§**有韧性**的日程表里预留了余量。
resistant§He was resistant to the idea for a year and then adopted it.§他**抵触**这个想法一年，随后采纳了它。
resolute§A resolute no on Monday saves five meetings.§周一一个**坚决**的“不”能省下五次会议。
resolve§Her resolve did not waver, and neither did the deadline.§她的**决心**没有动摇，截止日期也没有。
resonance§Resonance at that frequency shook the whole footbridge.§该频率的**共振**震动了整座人行桥。
